Fe — an extraverted feeling — is a judging function, so it delivers verdicts about the room instead of pure perceptions. Ti receives almost nothing that can be proven and remains inactive due to hunger. Real batteries alternate judgment with perception precisely so that something is always gathering material.

Ne — extraverted intuition, the auxiliary here — offers many parallel possibilities instead of established facts. You build broadly and provisionally: frameworks are drafted, tested, and discarded easily, including frameworks for situations that do not yet exist.
The grid becomes wide and airy, with entire wings raised and demolished in seconds.
the INTP combination
Long stillness, and suddenly the entire grid settles all at once.

Ni — introverted intuition — sends few inputs, each arriving already condensed into a single interpretation. Ti has little to test and much to arrange, reorganizing itself in its entirety around each arrival. No standard stack places Ni directly over Ti; this coupling is the site's own thought experiment.
a non-standard coupling

Sense — an extroverted sensation — delivers a fast and dense flow of what is physically present right now. Analysis is limited to what the object in front of you can confirm, and it is confirmed immediately. Problem-solving logic: short feedback loops, little theory.
The grid becomes narrow and heavy, thickening where the feeder lands.
the ISTP combination
The grid tightens without growing: the same joints welded again, the same rooms traversed over and over.

Yes — introverted perception, the tertiary function of the INTP — provides stored records instead of new perception. It presents you with old conclusions in the face of old data: it remains rigorous, increasingly isolated, because nothing that is being tested was gathered today. This is the loop, seen from the inside.
the loop coupling (Ti–Si, INTP under stress)

Where **Te** asks *"does it work?"* and builds external structures, **Ti** asks *"is it true?"* and builds internal coherence. Te trades elegance for speed; Ti trades speed for truth — a difference in what each is willing to pay, not in what each is capable of achieving.
Same element, opposite attitudes: one instrument oriented towards the world, the other towards its own functioning.

review.issue: The back-translation replaces 'Ti' (Jungian function) with 'IT' (Information Technology).
review.back: What the room sees: an agreement dismantled for the sake of sport. What is happening: You are loading a claim the way an engineer loads a bridge, because someone might have to stand on it. The tell is that the proof is symmetrical: offer an IT user a better attack on their own position and they will accept it with visible gratitude, something that no one who argues for sport has ever done.
Stress tests are the only way to weld a joint in the lattice.
You only argue for the sake of arguing.

A friend in mourning does not have a flawed model of the situation — and improving the model is the only move this function possesses natively. Your Ti dominant on a deathbed produces an impeccable root cause analysis, correct in every detail and erroneous in essence: the moment requires witnessing, not diagnosing. Mature Ti users learn to bring a different function to that door.
The grid waits in the car.
The condolence call

An ESFJ under prolonged stress suddenly becomes rigid and logical, arguing technicalities with an intensity that startles everyone, even themselves. This is the 'grip': an exhausted dominant function yielding control to the inferior Ti, which emerges without any of the calibrations of a practiced Ti.

Whether you are an INFJ or an ISFJ, it is the logic maintained as a garden rather than a residence: the flawless spreadsheet for the shared house, the private taxonomy of teas, the hermetic argument rehearsed and never delivered. It is abandoned halfway through the trial the moment someone in the room needs something; in this stack, coherence is a pleasure and harmony is a duty.

Under stress, an INTP's dominant Ti pairs with tertiary Si and begins to restate old conclusions with old data. Reasoning remains rigorous; the inputs cease to be new. Because both functions look inward, nothing in the pair can contradict it; the pattern that typology forums call a loop.
The loop
the loop

Both are cold and both say "that is incorrect," so the pair constantly collapses. Notice what closes a case. One closes it in results—decided, sent, next—and finds continuous analysis as something self-indulgent. The other reopens a settled matter at midnight because a definition is still shaky, and finds sending a shaky definition slightly scandalous. One optimizes the verdict; the other audits the reasoning that produced it.
Same cold surface, different machinery underneath.

review.back: Click a button to send an entry to you and watch how it tests, integrates, or reconstructs it around what arrives.
A new piece of data arrives — true, but not connected to anything that You currently possess. It is filed without forcing its adjustment; not every observation must find its place today.
The fact is situated next to the grid like an island, in its own color.
Two islands are already waiting. Ti tolerates loose facts, but longs for a bridge: try to discover a causal connection.
A candidate connection arrives: a small causal assertion that the parked fact is deduced from the things the model already contains. It is tested before something is merged.
Observe how the bridge extends from the grid towards the island...

The connection is maintained, so the fact ceases to be separate: from now on it is simply part of how the model says the world works. An approved verification is one of the few events that Ti registers as pleasure.
The peaks of pleasure increase, stress decreases, and the entire ensemble folds into the grid and disappears.
There is no island to connect to yet — A fact is observed first...
Ti — Introverted Thought · CURRENTS

In the second seat, Ti is activated deliberately rather than running by default. It edits instead of drafting: what the dominant perception function—the possibilities of Ne or the live readings of Se—provides is subjected to consistency tests before it is trusted. Rigor on demand, at a moderate cost.
The grid is displayed at four-fifths of its size and grows in sessions instead of doing so continuously.
An ENTP proposes six ideas and then silently dismantles four of them before anyone else can do so.

In the sixth seat, Ti turns inward like a debugger: sporadic and harsh audits of its own reasoning — "your definitions don't hold up" — delivered as verdicts rather than help. It inspects much more reliably than it constructs.
Brief red flashes cross a grid that is, otherwise, faint: inspection without construction.
An ISTJ rereads their own report at midnight and finds only carelessness, nothing of it specific enough to correct.
An inverted grid built downwards — a structure recruited for demolition.

The eighth seat is the rarest and the most costly to face. When there is an eruption—usually at the end of a bad streak—it produces a cold pseudology directed toward oneself: an argument about one's own uselessness, disguised as objectivity. It is the least practiced seat in the stack, not a hidden truth.
At 3 a.m., an INFP assembles a case that sounds airtight as to how every opportunity was wasted, complete with graphic evidence.

In the first seat, Ti functions without being turned on: every incoming assertion is tested against a private model of how things fit together, all day long, at low cost. Contradictions emerge quickly and cheaply. The price is the pace: an assertion is not usable until it is consistent, and consistency takes as long as it takes.
CURRENTS draws this as a full-size grid: large, fast, and silent, growing without visible effort.
A new article is read on Monday; nothing is said until Thursday, when a conclusion arrives that reorganizes the rest.
The grid draws in a small and slow way, with visible static — the connections fail and land heavily when they do.

review.issue: The term 'grip' was translated as 'claw', which changes the specific Jungian concept.
review.back: In the fourth seat, Ti has the highest cost per use and is used the least. In daily life, the person borrows others' frames instead of building their own; under prolonged stress, the seat can take control and produce a rigid all-or-nothing logic that doesn't sound like them — the eruption that Quenk calls the claw.
An ESFJ who has been the host all week suddenly argues a technicality tooth and nail, with a tone that surprises them both.

The fifth seat opens the shadow — the four positions that a person rarely executes, and mostly without noticing. Here, Ti awakens combatively: when the usual reasoning of Te of the person is challenged, definitions are questioned, and the logic of the critic is dismantled, in service of protecting the plan instead of investigating.
Below the rail's waterline, the grid fades and vibrates, assembling itself only when touched.
An ENTJ whose deployment is questioned spends ten minutes attacking the grammar of the question.
A medium-sized, bright grid where it is used and scarce in the rest.

In the tertiary seat, Ti is authentic but narrow: reliable in a few practiced domains, unreliable outside of them, and notably stronger with age. Under stress, it can pair with the dominant function to defend conclusions that no outsider can test — the pattern called the loop.
An ISFJ's spreadsheet is impeccable; that same rigor is never risked in a meeting.

In the seventh seat, the demands of formal consistency are recorded as traps rather than tools. The person evades them—with charm, absurdity, or a change of subject—and genuinely does not see the rule they are accused of breaking. The blindness is real, not tactical, and there is no malice in it.
The grid is drawn with missing pieces and does not close: the edges that should join do not do so.
When asked to admit that two of his statements conflict, an ESFP laughs, accepts both, and moves on.
